name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,335

entries.clue: Improper, like some letters in anagram clues? (3,2,5)

annotation.definition2: like some letters in anagram clues?

blocks.note: a plain sense: not acceptable, against the rules

blocks.clueFragment: like some letters in anagram clues?
blocks.note: the fodder of an anagram is printed with its letters in the wrong sequence

annotation.surface: A setter confesses that anagram clues are a bit improper.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful definition about crosswords themselves; the question mark flags that it is not a dictionary sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Both senses are idiomatic: a remark that breaks the rules of a meeting, and letters jumbled from their proper sequence.

entries.clue: Geolocations broadcast for scientist at sea (12)

indicatorNotes.broadcast: seeds broadcast are scattered in all directions, so the letters are scattered

annotation.surface: A research ship transmits its position for a scientist on board.
annotation.walkthrough: Every letter of the single long word is used; 'broadcast' reads as radio, which suits the surface and hides its real job.
annotation.definitionFit: An oceanologist studies the sea, so is a scientist whose work is at sea.

entries.clue: Potato, perhaps underground next to river (5)

indicatorNotes.next to: places the river letter right after the underground

blocks.note: the Tube is London's underground railway

annotation.surface: Potatoes growing underground beside a river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Underground' looks like the place a potato grows, but it is the London Underground, known as the Tube.
annotation.definitionFit: A potato is the best-known example of a tuber, hence 'perhaps'.

entries.clue: Distant ranch, miles away (3)

indicatorNotes.away: sends the M for miles out of the word

annotation.surface: An isolated ranch, many miles from anywhere.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'miles away' a phrase about distance, but it is an instruction: take M away from FARM.
annotation.definitionFit: Far and distant both mean a long way off.

entries.clue: Go about two (6)

annotation.surface: A terse instruction to wander around in twos.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is the formal sense of repair: to go somewhere, as in 'repair to the drawing room'.
annotation.definitionFit: A formal, rather old-fashioned sense of going somewhere, as in retiring after dinner to the library.

entries.clue: Absolve former partner on drug charge (9)

blocks.note: an ex is a former partner
a rate is a charge, a price

annotation.surface: Clearing an ex who has been accused of a drug offence.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charge' reads as a criminal accusation to match 'absolve', but it is the price sense: RATE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to clear someone of blame or guilt.

entries.clue: Good American folk wisdom in abundance (6)

blocks.note: lore is traditional knowledge passed among people

annotation.surface: Homespun American wisdom, of which there is plenty.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Folk wisdom' is a two-word block: LORE is the traditional knowledge handed down among ordinary people.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, though an unusual one: it follows its noun, as in 'prizes galore'.

entries.clue: Rather hot tea brewed for cosy chat (5,2,5)

indicatorNotes.brewed: brewing mixes ingredients into something new

annotation.surface: Making a pot of fairly hot tea ready for an intimate talk.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface fits perfectly: 'brewed' is what you do to tea, so the indicator hides in plain sight.
annotation.definitionFit: A heart-to-heart is a frank, intimate conversation.

entries.clue: One glowing stage manager finally accepting award (5)

indicatorNotes.finally: takes the final letter of each word
indicatorNotes.accepting: the outer letters take the award inside them

blocks.note: last letters of stagE and manageR
MBE = Member of the Order of the British Empire, an honour

annotation.surface: A stage manager, beaming, finally picks up an award.
annotation.walkthrough: E and R wrap around MBE. 'One glowing' looks like a happy winner but is the definition: a coal still alight. The MBE is a British honour given by the monarch.
annotation.definitionFit: An ember is a piece of coal or wood still glowing in a dying fire.

entries.clue: Fuel for aircraft lacking lead, primarily (7)

indicatorNotes.lacking: removes the letter from the aircraft

blocks.note: a plane is an aircraft; minus L it is PANE

annotation.surface: Fuel for planes running on unleaded.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fuel for aircraft' wants to be the definition, but only 'Fuel' is; 'for' is PRO. 'Lacking lead' sounds like unleaded petrol.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this bottled gas is burned in barbecues and heaters.

entries.clue: A king and queen appearing in local story (9)

indicatorNotes.appearing in: puts the royal letters inside the local word

annotation.surface: A king and queen turn up in a local tale.
annotation.walkthrough: King and queen both give R, from the Latin rex and regina; 'appearing in' reads as 'starring in', which suits the royal surface.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both are an account of connected events.

entries.clue: Discover drama is ultimately bound to happen (9)

indicatorNotes.ultimately: takes the final letter of each word before it

blocks.note: last letters of dramA and iS

annotation.surface: Finding out that a drama will inevitably take place.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Ultimately' reads as 'in the end', but it points back at the last letters of the two words before it.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both mean to find something out, with a sense of making sure.

entries.clue: Blade chops grass generally in the middle (3)

indicatorNotes.in the middle: takes the centre letter of each word

blocks.note: middle letters of chOps, grAss and geneRally

annotation.surface: A mower blade cutting grass, mostly through the centre of the lawn.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Blade' pairs so naturally with 'chops grass' that it reads as a mower or a blade of grass; it is an oar's blade. Each word has an odd length, so each has a single middle letter.
annotation.definitionFit: An oar is a long pole with a flat blade, and 'blade' can stand for the whole oar.

entries.clue: Somewhat ill, I lack colour (5)

indicatorNotes.Somewhat: only some of the words are used

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of 'ill' to just before the end of 'lack'

annotation.surface: Someone feeling a bit poorly and looking pale.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lack colour' reads as looking pale, which suits 'somewhat ill'; the definition is just 'colour'.
annotation.definitionFit: A pale purple named after the shrub's flowers.

entries.clue: Splendour of unusual result (6)

indicatorNotes.unusual: the letters are in an unusual order

annotation.surface: Admiring the brilliance of a surprise outcome.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Of' reads as part of a phrase, 'splendour of', but only joins the definition to the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym by extension: a soft shine, and figuratively glory or distinction.

entries.clue: Highly capable head of accounts department (5)

annotation.surface: Praise for a very competent head of the accounts department.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head of accounts department' reads as a job title, but 'head of' applies only to 'accounts'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: skilled, expert.

entries.clue: Gentle current job that’s easy? (6)

blocks.note: informal: a task done with no effort

annotation.surface: An undemanding job, like drifting on a gentle current.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current' suggests water or electricity; here it is air.
annotation.definitionFit: A breeze is both a light wind and, informally, a task done with no effort.

entries.clue: Fuel downturn experiencing a reverse (3)

indicatorNotes.experiencing a reverse: the word is turned back to front

blocks.note: a sag is a dip or downturn

annotation.surface: A slump in fuel prices that then goes into reverse.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like market news, with 'reverse' as a setback; it is the instruction to read SAG backwards.
annotation.definitionFit: Gas is a fuel, and in North America the word for petrol.

entries.clue: Element seldom encountered where we live (4,5)

annotation.surface: An element hardly ever found on our planet.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is nearly true, as rare earth elements are scarce in usable concentrations.
annotation.definitionFit: A rare earth is any of the lanthanide group of chemical elements.

entries.clue: Put up beams in an auditorium (5)

indicatorNotes.in an auditorium: an audience hears the word rather than reading it

annotation.surface: Rigging lighting beams in a theatre.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beams' suggests stage lights or timbers being hoisted; it is rays, which sound like the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to lift or erect, as a flag or a building.

entries.clue: Superficial person who’s good at riding waves (7)

blocks.note: to surf is to ride waves

annotation.surface: A shallow character whose only talent is surfing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Superficial person' reads as one phrase, but the definition is the adjective alone; 'person who's good at riding waves' is a surf ace.
annotation.definitionFit: Surface, as an adjective, means superficial: 'a surface impression'.

entries.clue: Land in area alongside church (5)

indicatorNotes.alongside: puts the church abbreviation next to IN A

annotation.surface: A plot of land next to a church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Land' reads as a building plot; it is a country.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a land in the sense of a country.

entries.clue: Chairs regularly missing wheels (3)

blocks.note: C h A i R s: the odd letters survive

annotation.surface: Wheelchairs that have lost their wheels.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wheels' is slang for a car, so the surface's wheelchair picture hides the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Wheels is informal for a car: 'nice wheels'.

entries.clue: Tender name misconstrued as expression of love (10)

indicatorNotes.misconstrued: the letters are put together wrongly

annotation.surface: A pet name taken the wrong way as a declaration of love.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tender name' already means an endearment, so the surface nearly defines the answer twice.
annotation.definitionFit: An endearment is a word or phrase expressing affection.
